title: Generic types in strongly minimal theories

based_on.title: Model Theory of Groups
based_on.pages: Definition 2.25 and Proposition 2.26, p.8 (revision 2018-05-21); arbitrary parameter-set argument expanded

summary: Construct the unique generic one-type over any parameter set and count algebraic types to prove omega-stability in a countable language.
abstract: In an infinite equality structure, an element either equals a named point or satisfies the one remaining complete description. Strong minimality extends this distinction from equality to every unary formula: each definable set is finite or has finite complement. All cofinite conditions fit together into one complete type, whose realizations are precisely the points outside algebraic closure of the parameters. Every other type is confined to a finite definable set and is already realized in the original model. Counting formulas bounds the algebraic closure and leaves only this one additional generic type. In a countable language there are therefore only countably many complete one-types over each countable parameter set, giving omega-stability under the one-variable counting convention.
